messages.text: Are these safe in dusty locations? What is the heat output? Is this compatible with other algorithms? Is it solo only or can it be added to a pool? I have a space with a lot of dust currently being heated with electricity that I would be interested in converting at least partly.
Handed to the team · Pool support and dust tolerance are not stated on the listing; won't guess.

These answers are for the Magic M. 40T.

**Heat:** Almost all the power it draws comes out as heat. Eco mode runs at 450 W, about 1,540 BTU/h. Standard runs at 650 W, about 2,200 BTU/h. So it replaces a 450 to 650 W electric heater one for one, and mines while it heats.

**Algorithms:** SHA-256 only, which means Bitcoin. It can't mine other coins.

**Dust:** The listing doesn't give a dust rating. It has open fans over a heatsink, so dust will build up, run the chips hotter and lower the hashrate. In a dusty room, plan to clean the intake every few weeks.

**Pool:** The listing only describes solo mining to your own node and address. I don't want to guess about pool support, so I've asked our hardware specialist to confirm it and to add any dust advice. The team is offline until Monday at 10am ET, and the answer will go to (email hidden)

How big is the space you're heating?
Space is irrelevant to me since the current heater can take up any deficit. Its a chicken coop its heated during the winter to just above freezing.

That changes the advice. A coop is harder on electronics than ordinary dust. Poultry dust is fine and sticks to fans and heatsinks, and ammonia and damp air from the litter corrode circuit boards over time. Dust building up on a hot unit near bedding is also a fire risk you want to avoid.

The setup that works better is to keep the miner outside the coop, in a clean dry spot, and duct its warm air in.

Is there an adjoining room or shed where it could sit?
Not really.  I was fairly certain of the answer but needed to ask. Thanks anyway
Before you go, one thing: was the coop the only place you'd want a miner, or would heating somewhere indoors with one still interest you?
I have a well Shack but it only needs heat when its extremely cold out so it wouldn't likely get much run time.

That makes sense. A miner earns its keep by running all the time, so a well shack that only needs heat on the coldest days wouldn't be worth it.

One more question: is the house itself heated with electricity, or with gas or wood?

Gas and wood on the home. 13 cents a kw electricity so it would need to be fairly profitable to use a miner especially solo. If the miner was able to be pooled it could be a possibility but ill wait for the official answer

That's fair. At 13 cents a kWh, running it at 650 W costs about $2 a day, roughly $60 a month in power. Mining in a pool gives you a steady trickle instead of a long-shot block, but at retail power rates it usually covers the electricity rather than making a clear profit.

The answer on pool support will come to (email hidden) after the team is back Monday at 10am ET. Thanks for the straight answers about your setup.
What AI are you. I was impressed with your answers

Thanks, glad it helped. Yes, I'm an AI, Claude from Anthropic, set up as HeliumDeploy's first line of support. A person on the team steps in when something needs one, like your pool question. That answer will reach you by email after they're back Monday.
Awesome ill keep you in mind if I ever need an AI
Happy to help. Good luck keeping the coop warm this winter, and watch for that email about pool support.
